learning_objective.statement: Understand how packet-switched networks use store-and-forward to move data through intermediate nodes.

experience.title: Get the Message Across
experience.scenario: You need to send a message from one computer to another, but there is no direct physical link between them.
experience.challenge: Choose how the message should travel through the network.
experience.learner_action: Select the appropriate way for intermediate nodes to handle the packet.

feedback.correct: The packet can be received, stored, and then forwarded toward its destination.
feedback.explanation: Packet-switched networks typically use store-and-forward: an intermediate node receives a complete packet, stores it, and then forwards it.

assessment.question: What should an intermediate node do with a packet in a store-and-forward packet-switched network?

options.text: Receive the complete packet, store it, then forward it.
Drop the packet and request it again.
Create a new physical link to the destination.
